front.title: Chain-Agnostic Anchoring of Canonical Settlement References for Agentic Payments

abstract.t:
This document specifies how a canonical content-addressed settlement reference is anchored into a transaction on any blockchain, uniformly across chain families, so that the same agentic-payment settlement can be recorded on-chain and later verified offline from the transaction bytes alone.
The settlement reference is a SHA-256 digest over the JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS, RFC 8785) form of a settlement record. This document does not redefine the digest; it defines (1) a chain identification rule that rejects ambiguous chain names before a settlement is bound to a network, and (2) a family-uniform anchor encoding that places the reference in the one field each chain family makes available for opaque data (EVM calldata or a log topic, an SVM memo, an AVM note, a UTXO OP_RETURN output, or a generic metadata carrier). The anchor carries only the digest; it carries no party identifiers, amounts, or personal data in cleartext.
Because the reference is content-addressed and the encoding is fixed per family, any holder of the settlement record can recompute the reference, read the anchor from the on-chain field, and confirm the two match with no call to the settling party and no chain-specific verification logic beyond reading one field.
